title: Any word on the next RPG Maker version?

posts.author: LunarFlareStudios
posts.body:
I'm not sure what's next for RPG Maker after Unite failed so hard... but that makes me super uneasy. I hear rumors of Kadokawa being bought by Sony, and that also scares me. I can only hope that a new RPG Maker comes out in 2025!
So, uh, I'm searching everywhere on Google, but I want to ask you in case there's anything I overlooked while searching (I'll even search again after posting this). Has there been any word or news of any kind concerning when the next standalone RPG Maker will come out? And what will come of RPG Maker if the rumors of Kadokawa's acquisition are true?
I'm just so scared. I love RPG Maker and I hope all goes well for it.
(Also if this is in the wrong thread, the mods are more than welcome to put this post where it belongs.)

This isn't a rumor, this is true. However, the acquisition has to be approved by the courts first, so no acquisition has been made, simply Sony has said "We want to do that." and, just like Microsoft with Activision, it will spend a long time in the courts before being approved.
LunarFlareStudios said:
what will come of RPG Maker if the rumors of Kadokawa's acquisition are true?
Click to expand...
Depends on Sony, and the courts. Technically speaking, part of Microsoft's acquisition of Activision was that they were not allowed to disband any studio or lay off any staff as part of the acquisition. That didn't stop them from finding a loop hole by saying things like Tango Gameworks and Arcane Austin's previous games were "under performing" and erased those studios from existence.
But, the point is that it depends on the courts and Sony.
Sony may deem the Maker arm not profitable and sever it. But, my wager would be on it not being significant enough for them to care. Kadokawa owns a lot of great properties, such as Bandai Namco, as well as a huge amount of anime and manga. So Sony likely wants them for these names that generate millions of dollars per quarter. Even GGG at it's best still likely makes sales that are a drop in the bucket by comparison. They may just not care about GGG, or they may just give them an amicable release of contract to go solo.
Now, whether GGG can hold their own solo has yet to be determined, though with the piss-poor updates to MZ/MV and Unite's quality, the barometer is leaning towards them - to use another forum members words - "lack[ing] business sense".
However, saying you are "scared" seems to be a bit of a hyperbole. These are just softwares. Your life is not at risk by any of this.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
It is imho very unlikely that they go for a subscription model.
Because there is a difference between the maker and all those programs that switched to a subscription model, and that is the project length/workload.
In Word, Photoshop or similar programs most or every single project (picture, book, etc) can be done in weeks or rarely months. A game needs a minimum of a lot of months, often several years to complete.
And while Office or Photoshop is used by a lot of professionals, the maker still targets the independent or hobby developer instead of professionals.
And if you spread the cost of the editor over thirty month or so, the subscription per month would be extremely low to the point of having more banking fees that anything else.
A higher cost for the editor on the other hand would be a problem for the target customer.
Subscription Services are mostly valid if the cost for the program is/was above 1000$ with an expected update/replacement every two or three years - RM has a cost around 100$ and an expected life of 5+ years in comparison.

I think if they made a new version that was compatible with MZ and to some extent MV, and had the following features:
A full interface editor for boxes and menus

posts.author: Eternidade_1
posts.body:
I think using RPG Maker for a 3D interface is a lot, after all, its previous versions were 2D graphics.
In this sense, an isometric support, or 2.5D, is much more logical.
Isometric
The isometric perspective is a rendering technique where the observer's point of view is at an angle in which the three dimensions (height, width and depth) are equally represented.
Examples of games that use this technique include "Diablo II" and "SimCity 2000".
2.5D
The term "2.5D" refers to a rendering style that mixes two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) elements. Basically, characters and objects can be drawn in 2D, but the scenery or environment has a three-dimensional depth, or vice versa.
Following the path of games, comes isometric, 2.5 and finally 3D. Taking these prerequisites into account, we can have up to 3 new versions of rpg maker.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I don't want to see any new perspectives in RPG Maker. Might be egoistic, as I wouldn't use those, but it would turn RPG Maker into 3 engines at once.
All commands are way harder to use, as you'd always have to think about it like "in classic mode, it does this, in isometric it works different, and in 3D not at all". There are so much more commands needed, to have the same control over a 3D or 2.5D perspective.
If you split them completely, to have only relevant commands, you'd have 3 softwares in one. So you need 3x of developers. You need way more artists, as every graphic needs an RTP.
This would increase the price of development, and thus the price of the RPG Maker. I don't want to spend $300+ for an RPG Maker that comes with 3D support I won't use.
I want to see all the development focussing on the one RPG Maker, without trying to be something different.
Just one example, give more control over event conditions.
Only one variable? Only ">="?
We're always dancing around these restrictions that haven't been touched since RM2k.
I would love to stack as many conditions as I want, like HUD Maker Ultra does.

posts.author: Monad
posts.body:
I feel GGG has always been focused on keeping their mainline engine reliably accessible, staying away from too high tech that make them less accessible. The format they use now, buy a full RM engine like a full game no strings attached, and DLC later if you want it, is pretty reliable and fits long term use for devs.
They’ve had side stuff experiments before, like the 3D console RMs. They didn’t overtake over the mainline RMs, so I don’t see things like Unite or With as attempts to replace it for some kind of bigger instant audience.
Before a new maker engine, I think GGG should totally scrap and redo how they are doing RTP, I personally really don’t like the MV/MZ “panime” art style, and the Komodo plaza pounding out 20 heroine generator parts every hour and a new grass tile pack (I’m really exaggerating) makes it look like that’s all it can do from an outside perspective. (I do think it can look good for devs who actually like it though) I think it would be a bigger transformation than redoing the whole RM engine again, and it’s overlooked too much.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Komodo Plaza doesn't make the DLC, some random artist does and they just publish and advertise it on their channels and take a cut. They're not even exclusive publishers because you can usually find the same DLC on itch or Gamedevmarket, etc. There are submission forms for you to submit your own.
RPG Maker's selling point is ease of use (you can make games without knowing any programming, even though "eventing" is basic programming with a coat of paint). Maybe price too for the older engines when they're on sale for less than $15. It's not that versatile without 3rd party plugins.
Their new installments are going to struggle without the years of 3rd party plugins MV and MZ has. They're too expensive and too restrictive.

merging the battle system with eventing so people could more easily make their own systems, things like memorize map could be used normally, and just having an option to load a preset battle system setup like current one.
A menus customizer, RPGs need many kinds of menus!
A Catalog system where you could make an ID array where you can put anything into the ID slots: bgm, face graphics, parallax backgrounds, and have “catalog call” options that would call the material. So you could store face graphics into a catalog and call them by a variable input for example.
Making all equipment slots general and based of the equipment types instead
Redoing the tileset system, things like height and underpassing, and having a tileset merger (I wish the current makers had an autotile and shadow auto/manual switch)
More movement options like chase event (can be done with script calls pretty easy though) and queued moving
Edit: oh and grouping system/group call for anything with an ID array
I don’t think even the best RM games scratched the surface of what it can really make, and The whole “You can’t make games without plugins” mentality kind of backfires what RM is made for.

It's not whether you can afford it or not. It's the value proposition compared to its competitors. If the competition is free (Godot) or free until you publish commercially (GameMaker) then RPG Maker has to provide a lot more value to be worth it.
Can you make a game without plugins? Sure, the console RPG Makers don't have plugins. But you're a lot more limited in what you can do. You can't even change the menu without plugins.
